claims.text: The material family is multiphase AlxCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys with 1 ≤ x ≤ 2.
These alloys will undergo a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during aging at 400–600 °C.
The as-cast or homogenized initial state contains FCC, BCC, and incipient B2 ordered phases.
The initial microstructure has a disordered or short-range-ordered matrix, a ductile FCC phase, and a harder BCC/B2 phase.
Aging at 400–600 °C for 100–1000 hours drives an SRO-to-B2-LRO transition followed by B2 precipitate coarsening.
The density and connectivity of B2 ordered domains control their effectiveness as obstacles to dislocation motion.
Initial aging increases chemical-order density and thereby increases yield strength while reducing ductility.
Ordering embrittles the alloy by pinning dislocations, impeding cross-slip, and promoting cleavage in B2.
At intermediate aging times, a fully ordered and sufficiently continuous B2 phase causes brittle fracture and a ductility minimum.
Prolonged aging causes Ostwald ripening of B2 precipitates, reducing obstacle density and allowing Orowan looping or cross-slip.
A reversion of the matrix toward a more disordered state during prolonged aging could restore ductility.
Activation of twinning or localized shear banding could bypass ordered obstacles and restore ductility.
Elongation to failure will decrease from above 20% to below 5% and then recover to approximately 10–15% with increasing aging time.
The ductility minimum will likely occur after 100–300 hours of aging at approximately 400–500 °C.
Yield strength will initially increase and then plateau or decrease slightly with further aging.
As-cast AlxCoCrFeNi alloys typically have elongation above 20% because of a disordered FCC matrix and limited ordering.
The ordering-onset temperature depends strongly on Al content and ranges from approximately 1220 °C at x = 1 to 1850 °C at x = 2.
Ordering kinetics relevant to the ductility transition are significant at 400–600 °C despite limited diffusion.
The transition should be most pronounced for 1 ≤ x ≤ 1.5 because B2 is significant but not dominant enough to cause immediate as-cast brittleness.
